text.content:
Trigger: Any scene in which the character is not the center of attention.

Some ghouls and Cainites sublimate the urge to escape their circumstances, or come to believe their new powers entitle them to a certain amount of attention. Those who develop histrionics must be center stage in all situations: they affect extreme but shallow emotions, or dress and behave provocatively. Each scene, a histrionic character must spend a point of Willpower to avoid seeking the spotlight in some way; if the quest for recognition fails, she cannot spend Willpower and suffers a three-Trait penalty to resist frenzy for the rest of the scene.

Vampires develop this derangement as readily as ghouls: a childe might subconsciously rebel against an indifferent sire, an elder lacking the status implied by his age might become obsessed with being noticed, or a Nosferatu might overcompensate for his hideous appearance or for spending too much time Obfuscated. Ghouls and revenants raised amid a Tzimisce domitor's cruelty are especially prone to this fixation. This derangement is not a license to hog every scene and write it off as roleplaying — play it as the emotional disorder it is, hypersensitive to the opinions of others rather than oblivious to them.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Tzimisce, Chapter Two: Ego and Evolution
